title: Compact evidence briefs and compact audit index PRD (draft)
content:
Overview:

This PRD proposes an implementation for two adjacent features used by Private deployments: 1) compact, human-readable evidence briefs ("evidence briefs") that summarize an incident/change for customer operators and auditors; and 2) a compact audit index (index) that provides a small, efficient lookup layer for evidence items to support fast queries, exports, and legal holds. The goal is to provide forensically-sound artifacts that are compact (small storage footprint), human-consumable, and compatible with customer-managed networking and KMS constraints.

Problem and motivation:

Customers using Redwood Private frequently ask for: fast exports of incident evidence for legal/compliance, short human summaries that can be consumed by security teams, and a low-cost way to retain searchable pointers for long retention windows. Current full-archive approach stores large forensic bundles (full logs, pcap-like captures, and raw JSON) which are expensive to retain and slow to search. Operators also lack a standard, readable artifact to hand to customer SOCs during triage.

High-level goals:

- Create a "compact evidence brief": a short, signed document (~1-3KB typical) that summarizes a single event/change/approval with canonical metadata and a human-readable narrative.
- Provide a compact audit index: a minimal, compressed index record for every evidence brief that supports fast faceted queries (time, customer id, operator id, approval gate, outcome, canonical-hash).
- Ensure artifacts are cryptographically linked to canonical forensic bundles (hash pointers) to preserve chain-of-custody without duplicating heavy payloads.
- Respect customer-managed networking and KMS constraints: artifacts should be exportable and encryptable with customer keys and enable offline handover.

Non-goals:

- This is not a replacement for full forensic archive. We still keep full raw captures separately (configurable retention).
- Not intended to provide a full SIEM integration at launch; we will expose exports that customers can ingest into their SIEMs.

Primary personas and user stories:

- Customer SOC lead (Alice): "When an approval gate unexpectedly fails, I want a one-pager that explains what changed and provides a signed pointer to the raw evidence so I can quickly decide escalation."
- Redwood operator (Ben): "During a support call, I can generate and attach an evidence brief to the ticket so the customer sees a consistent summary without requesting full logs."
- Compliance auditor (External): "I want a compact index to pull all approval-gate failures for Q4 to validate our attestation sampling."

Functional requirements (must-have):

1) Brief structure: each evidence brief must include: TTL-limited human summary (text), event type (approval/change/rollback/incident), timestamp (ISO8601), customer_id, operator_id (if applicable), route/model reference, policy id (if applies), outcome (approved/denied/rolled-back/auto-failed), canonical-hash pointer to the corresponding forensic bundle, signature (service KMS or customer KMS), and minimal tags.

2) Index record: per-evidence index entry must include: canonical-hash, brief_uri (signed short-lived URL for retrieval), time-bucket (YYYY-MM-DD), outcome, gate-id, customer_id, and a compact attribute bitmask for fast faceting. Index should be stored in a columnar, compressed store optimized for TTL scans.

3) API: admin API to list/query index records with filters (time-range, customer, gate, outcome, operator) and to fetch a brief by canonical-hash. Export API to generate a signed export bundle (brief + pointer to raw evidence + signed export manifest).

4) Export format: signed NDJSON package for briefs + manifest that contains KMS-wrapped keys when required. Support gzipped TAR for customer downloads.

5) Keying: brief and manifest signatures must be optionally customer-KMS-wrapped on Private deployments. When customer-managed-KMS is present, we must support wrapping signatures or providing signed hashes in a way that preserves customer custody.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):

- Size: average brief should be <= 4KB; index entry <= 256 bytes (after compression).
- Query latency: index queries for a single customer across a 90-day window should return first-page (100 items) in < 500ms p95 for Dedicated/Private control-plane queries.
- Throughput: handle up to 200 new index records/sec per region for a large Private customer.

Data model (flat fields):

- brief_id (UUID string)
- canonical_hash (hex string, SHA256)
- event_type (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601 string)
- customer_id (string)
- operator_id (string)
- route_or_model (string)
- policy_id (string)
- outcome (string)
- summary_text (short string, 512–2048 chars recommended)
- tags (list of short strings)
- signed_manifest_uri (string)

Operator/customer UX flows (draft):

A) Operator flow (support console):
- Support opens an incident / ticket -> selects "Generate evidence brief" -> system pre-populates with event metadata -> operator can add narrative notes -> preview shows signed header + canonical-hash -> generate -> brief stored and index entry created -> link inserted into ticket and optionally emailed to customer (short-lived signed link).

B) Customer flow (Console/Api):
- Customer queries audit index with filters -> sees brief metadata (summary preview) -> requests full brief -> if customer KMS is configured, they must provide a retrieval assertion; otherwise short-lived signed URL is returned.

Retention, exports, and legal hold:

- Evidence briefs: default retention 2 years (configurable per-customer; minimum 90 days).
- Index: default retention 7 years (customer configurable). Index entries are compact and do not contain full raw data, enabling longer retention at lower cost.
- Legal hold: when a customer opens a legal hold, index records and corresponding canonical-hash pointers become immutable and retention overridden to indefinite until release. Exports for legal holds must include signed manifest, briefs, and raw-evidence pointers; we provide an 'evidence-packaging' tool to assemble a forensics bundle for transfer.

Security and compliance considerations:

- Chain-of-custody: canonical-hash links raw forensic bundles to briefs; signatures (service or customer KMS) provide tamper-evidence.
- PII minimization: briefs should avoid including sensitive payloads; include only metadata + human summary. Raw evidence remains in full archive protected by existing controls.
- Auditability: all brief generations must be themselves recorded in an immutable event stream (append-only) with operator identity.

Storage and cost estimate (rough):

- Estimates assume average 3KB per brief and an index growth of 20M rows/year across all Private customers. Storage cost for briefs: ~60GB/year; index (compressed): ~5GB/year. These are order-of-magnitude numbers; infra team to validate.

Implementation notes (engineering constraints):

- Index store candidates: clickhouse-like columnstore, DynamoDB with compressed attributes, or a managed OLAP (e.g., Bigtable + secondary columnar store). Need to prototype p95 latency with sample workloads.
- Signature path: integrate with customer-KMS plugin used for key wrapping in Private. If customer KMS not present, use Redwood signing key and provide certificate chain for downstream verification.

Rollout plan (staged):

1) Prototype: implement brief generation and local index using existing control-plane storage; internal-only UI for support (2 sprints).
2) Beta with 2–3 Private customers: add customer-KMS wrapping, export tooling, legal-hold path (3 sprints).
3) GA: console UX polish, performance tuning for index, SLA targets, runbook and run rate contracts (4 sprints).

Success metrics (initial):

- Time-to-provide brief during support call: < 120s median (after generation action).
- Customer satisfaction on first beta customers (CSAT) >= 4/5 for evidence provisioning.
- Index query p95 < 500ms for 90-day queries (single-customer).

Open questions / risks (to discuss):

- How do we handle multi-tenant aggregation where a single event touches multiple customer tenants? (Edge case: shared infra incidents).
- Should briefs include obfuscated excerpts of payloads for faster triage? Trade-off with PII/minimization.
- Long-term operational cost of legal holds if many customers use indefinite retention.
- Compatibility and UX around customer-managed KMS flows when customers use offline HSMs.

Next steps / action items:

- [Product] Align with legal and privacy on PII policies for summary_text (owner: Maya; due 2024-12-12).
- [Eng] Spike: prototype index with ClickHouse mock and load test at 100k rows/simulated queries (owner: Diego; due 2024-12-20).
- [Security] Review signing model with customer-KMS options and provide threat model (owner: Rafael; due 2025-01-05).
- [Support] Draft internal support templates and ticket automation actions for evidence brief workflow (owner: Nora; due 2024-12-18).

Notes to reviewers:

- This draft prioritizes small, signed artifacts that are friendly to human triage and long-term low-cost retention. It intentionally keeps raw forensic data out of the index records but preserves a verifiable pointer.
- Feedback requested on: recommended index store, default retention windows, and signature approaches for customer KMS.

Quick checklist (work-in-progress):

- [ ] Finalize brief JSON schema
- [ ] Design index compression and bitmask attribute map
- [ ] Add API auth model for brief retrieval under customer-KMS
- [ ] Write exported bundle manifest spec
- [ ] Prepare beta customer list and runbooks

End of draft.
